messages:
katie: hitting ~30% of prod deploys failing in GH Actions last hour, all with 401 from the Redwood API. started ~10:03UTC.
katie: sample job log:
```
2026-03-15T10:03:12Z ERROR deploy failed status=401 body={\"error\":\"unauthorized\",\"message\":\"token expired or invalid\"}
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CI_SA_TOKEN' https://api.redwood.com/v1/deploys
```
katie: this token is a short-lived impersonation token we mint in the runner init step. not seen before today.

devops-bot: :warning: deploy-pipeline #canary reported 401s x5 in 6m (alert: ci-deploy-401-rate)

mohit: can you paste the token creation command or workflow step? also check runner clock (clock skew is super common with VMs).

katie: workflow step snippet:
```
- name: mint ci token
  run: |
    TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=ci-deployer@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --audiences=redwood-api --ttl=600)
    echo "CI_SA_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_ENV
```

katie: running on self-hosted fleet (k8s runners) — just did `date` on one of the failing pods: `Mon Mar 15 10:08:33 UTC 2026` (real time is 10:03:40). so runner is ~5m fast.

mohit: yep that's the issue. Redwood API validates iat/exp windows tightly for impersonation tokens; if your clock is ahead tokens can appear not yet valid or already expired depending on skew.

mohit: quick repro check: from a runner with skewed clock run:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.com/v1/health
# if clock skew > TTL you'll see 401 / invalid_token
```

katie: confirmed — after syncing time with `sudo ntpdate -u pool.ntp.org` the same job completed successfully.

support-lead: thanks for debugging. two followups:
1) short-term: add a sanity check in the runner bootstrap to `ntpstat`/`chronyc tracking` and exit early with a clear error if skew > 60s.
2) medium-term: CI team should add jitter/retry around token mint + call (we can't always avoid every skew) and consider extending impersonation TTL to 15m for self-hosted runners.

al: Agreed. I'll open an infra ticket to add the bootstrap time check and a Grafana alert for runner-clock-skew > 90s. Also we'll update the GH Action template with recommended `chrony` install snippet.

ci-eng: sample snippet for bootstrap (we'll add to base image):
```
# ensure chrony running and sync
apt-get update && apt-get install -y chrony || true
chronyd -q 'pool pool.ntp.org iburst' || true
chronyc makestep || true
```

mohit: note: increasing TTL reduces sensitivity to skew but makes token window larger (attack surface). balance with retries and clock checks. For now 15m for self-hosted runners + 60s bootstrap check seems fine.

katie: added to our release checklist. will patch runners and re-run canary.

devops-bot: :white_check_mark: canary deployment now green after runner sync (10:22UTC).

support-lead: filing internal follow-up: INFRA-1247 "runner clock drift detection + CI token guidance". tagging security for TTL guidance.

katie: thanks all :pray: saved a lot of noise.
